title: The Rogue Planet That Steals Our Comets
hook: A hidden world in the Oort cloud is yanking icy bodies toward Earth, and we only found it by accident.
why_this_can_go_viral: Suggests a secret menace lurking at the edge of the solar system, feeding fears of unseen cosmic dangers.

title: The Star That Cannibalized Its Own Solar System
hook: A white dwarf was caught devouring the remains of its own planets, leaving a graveyard of metal and rock.
why_this_can_go_viral: Anthropomorphic horror of a star eating its children; visceral and scientifically shocking.

title: The Dark Matter Signal That Vanished Instantly
hook: A brief flash from an underground detector could have been dark matter—or something far stranger that erased itself.
why_this_can_go_viral: The mystery of a fleeting, unexplained detection plays on the 'almost found it' psychological tension.

title: The Extinction Event That Left a Scar on the Ocean Floor
hook: A massive impact crater under the Pacific is linked to a near-extinction, but no one knows where the asteroid went.
why_this_can_go_viral: A geological ghost story—evidence of destruction without a weapon—fuels conspiracy and disaster fascination.

title: The Classified 'NRO Satellite 47'—A Black Budget Telescope
hook: A spy satellite turned out to be the most powerful telescope ever built, aimed not at Earth but at deep space threats.
why_this_can_go_viral: Reveals secret government technology used for cosmic monitoring, blending espionage with astronomy.

title: The Rogue Star That's Heading Straight for Us
hook: A hypervelocity star is on a collision course with the solar system—and it will arrive within 5,000 years.
why_this_can_go_viral: Imminent stellar impact triggers primal fear of celestial annihilation with a tangible timeline.

title: The Fermi Paradox Tomb—A Message That Died Mid-Transmission
hook: Astronomers caught a signal that cut off abruptly, followed by silence—as if the sender was killed while broadcasting.
why_this_can_go_viral: Murder mystery in space—the story of a civilization that may have been silenced mid-sentence.

title: The Star That Spits Out Antimatter Bullets
hook: A neutron star fires jets of antimatter that explode on contact with normal matter—and one barely missed us.
why_this_can_go_viral: Antimatter is inherently terrifying; the idea of invisible bullets from space is pure sci-fi horror.

title: The Dark Matter Node That Warps Our GPS
hook: GPS satellites keep glitching over a specific patch of ocean—scientists think a clump of dark matter is bending time.
why_this_can_go_viral: Blends everyday technology failure with an invisible cosmic cause—relatable and mind-bending.

title: The Asteroid That Hit a Nuclear Waste Dump
hook: A small asteroid struck a classified waste facility—releasing radiation that could be mistaken for a nuclear attack.
why_this_can_go_viral: Nightmare scenario of cosmic event triggering a man-made disaster; high drama and dread.

title: The Extinction Comet That Came From Another Solar System
hook: Oumuamua's twin was not a rock—it was a comet from interstellar space that nearly ended all life 10,000 years ago.
why_this_can_go_viral: Connects a real visitor to a forgotten apocalypse—bridges mystery with historical disaster.

title: The Classified 'Project Orion'—A Starship Powered by Nukes
hook: In the 1960s, the US secretly designed a spaceship that would ride atomic explosions—until it was buried forever.
why_this_can_go_viral: Audacious, dangerous, and hidden—humanity's most powerful rocket idea taps into forbidden tech fascination.

title: The Fermi Paradox Scream—A Signal of Pure Terror
hook: A broadcast from a distant galaxy contains a pattern of rising panic—as if a civilization was recording its own end.
why_this_can_go_viral: Elicits existential dread and empathy for a dying alien race—emotionally charged and unforgettable.

title: The Rogue Black Hole That Eats from the Inside Out
hook: A black hole is devouring its host galaxy from the core—and it's moving toward the Milky Way faster than we thought.
why_this_can_go_viral: An unstoppable cosmic predator heading our way—pure sci-fi nightmare that is scientifically real.

title: The Star That Blinks Like a Cosmic Lighthouse—But Something Controls It
hook: A star dims and brightens with perfect precision every 2.3 hours—as if an artificial object is orbiting it.
why_this_can_go_viral: Reignites the 'alien megastructure' obsession with a new, more precise example—mystery that demands explanation.

title: The Extinction Meteor That Was a Sniper Shot
hook: Analysis shows an extinction-level impact was aimed from a specific direction—as if it was deliberately guided.
why_this_can_go_viral: Suggests cosmic assassination—an extinction event with intent, terrifyingly plausible.

title: The Classified 'Project Wintermark'—A Secret Moon Base
hook: Declassified documents reveal a joint US-Soviet plan to build a military outpost on the dark side of the moon in 1972.
why_this_can_go_viral: Romance of the forbidden moon base—taps into the enduring myth of a hidden lunar presence.

title: The Dark Matter That Stole the Stars
hook: A cluster of stars vanished from view overnight—dark matter absorbed their light, and we don't know why.
why_this_can_go_viral: Borrows from 'disappearance' mystery genre applied to space—creates a cosmic whodunit.

title: The Signal That Was a Silent Movie
hook: A radio signal from Proxima Centauri contained a visual sequence—a grainy film showing a planet dying.
why_this_can_go_viral: Combines signal mystery with visual storytelling—a cosmic snuff film that shocks and fascinates.

title: The Fermi Paradox Algorithm—A Formula That Predicts Our Death
hook: A mathematician created a model that calculates exactly when a civilization destroys itself—and we're past the deadline.
why_this_can_go_viral: Appeals to apocalyptic curiosity and data-driven fear—a 'clock is ticking' narrative that feels urgent.

title: The Asteroid That Appeared and Disappeared in One Hour
hook: A near-Earth object materialized on radar, then vanished an hour later—as if it was never there.
why_this_can_go_viral: Mysterious appearance and disappearance creates a 'glitch in the matrix' effect—instantly shareable.
